searchText: I'd like to bring this up again. Thoughts on removing **peer** sampling from the specs for Fulu? If we want to remove this, we can/should make a PR soon & make a final decision at the upcoming ACDC call. We want to remove **peer** sampling, not sampling right? whats the reason of wanting to remove peer sampling? Because nobody implements it? lmao thats not a good enough reason to remove it? Do we actually not need peer sampling? I thought the whole idea of reliable DA was the fact that we have peer sampling yeah We replaced peer sampling by custody sampling. All clients implement custody sampling i can give a pr? now that we have consensus over this it's a whole new area of tuning, research, implementation and devnet testing that i don't think anyone would want to get their hands dirty on at the moment. the whole idea of reliable DA was the fact that we have ~~peer~~ sampling. ==> Not especially peer sampling. Custody sampling does the job as well. custody sampling is implemented by all right? Yes, updated my message. think it would be best to have a pr already so that we can point ppl at it <@592004585506340885> going ahead with the pr Great, thank you 🙏 I always had an impression that research folks intentionally had peer sampling because it added some security guarantees. I think we should be happy to remove peer sampling as long as the protocol security does not suffer. is peer sampling something that you guys have implemented? if we have even a single client implementation, then we should keep it as "MAY", and we shouldn't remove it imo we have it, we have tests for it, but we don't use it no, not yet i don't see the need entirely, also with getBlobsV2 in place and strong guarantees of data column retrieval while the slot is advancing, and vals are attesting during sync, i'm pretty sure some of the clients, use a _form_ peer sampling in some way or the other. cc <@531934490826768418> ? just that the sampling frequencies may not follow any probabilistic nature, as given in spec by `get_extended_sample_count` https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4393 here we go Do you mean about https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4394? It doesn't really add much in terms of security guarantees, it's just in principle more efficient with bandwidth because it's through req/resp rather than gossip. The idea of having that spec was to allow clients to implement it whenever, to replace the "extra custody sampling" (the 4 additional custody groups over the minimum of 4) with something cheaper. I don't mind either way, as long as we don't treat that spec as something in the critical path of Fusaka (e.g. something that needs to be tested) OK, and in terms of number of custody columns - do we increase it if we drop the peer sampling? Nothing changes, we need a minimum of 8 samples, obtained in whatever way How would people feel about increasing `BALANCE_PER_ADDITIONAL_CUSTODY_GROUP`, say to 128 or 256, pushing up quite a bit the minimum stake to be a backbone node (I'll try for a bit with this <:crazycry:932693133546889216>), and making the impact even lower on nodes without a lot of validators? (e.g. with 128 you'd need at least 1024 ETH to go over the minimum of 8 columns, and you'd need 512 validators to be a backbone node) <@755590043632140352> had thoughts on this too OK, so it doesnt become less secure. you mean in FULU? or glamsterdam its a super late change for fulu imho it's not, we don't have a single validator custody devnet run (entirely) yet i mean it's not super late For now I'd just like to hear what people think about it generally 😄 In general I believe this is a good idea, previous to CSM the stake distribution of nodes was bimodal, with either 1-2 or really a lot. I suspect that CSM may have changed this slightly. At any rate my interest on the topic is that this numbers allow us to do statistics on the number of nodes that are expected to hold all columns and use this on our basic assumptions about DA, I know it's not as theoretically robust as saying there are x% chances that > 50% were assigned missing data, but I still think that this is just the same for all practical purposes. seems generally reasonable/positive. the discourse around this has been usually assuming a mostly, yeah, bimodal distribution, and this would push things towards that being descriptively true so if the design assumptions/analysis is oriented around that anyway, better to make the spec reflect that How would we feel about merging this PR soon & including it in the next release? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3510 I would like to follow up with PR that adds `SLOT_TIME_MS` too. Note we would not remove `SECONDS_PER_SLOT` from the config; maybe do that later, after fusaka.

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: I'd like to bring this up again. Thoughts on removing **peer** sampling from the specs for Fulu? If we want to remove this, we can/should make a PR soon & make a final decision at the upcoming ACDC call.

the whole idea of reliable DA was the fact that we have ~~peer~~ sampling.

excerpts.content: I always had an impression that research folks intentionally had peer sampling because it added some security guarantees. I think we should be happy to remove peer sampling as long as the protocol  security does not suffer.

excerpts.content: i don't see the need entirely, also with getBlobsV2 in place and strong guarantees of data column retrieval

excerpts.author: fradamt
excerpts.content: It doesn't really add much in terms of security guarantees, it's just in principle more efficient with bandwidth because it's through req/resp rather than gossip. The idea of having that spec was to allow clients to implement it whenever, to replace the "extra custody sampling" (the 4 additional custody groups over the minimum of 4) with something cheaper.

excerpts.author: fradamt
excerpts.content: I don't mind either way, as long as we don't treat that spec as something in the critical path of Fusaka (e.g. something that needs to be tested)

excerpts.author: sauliusgrigaitis
excerpts.content: OK, and in terms of number of custody columns - do we increase it if we drop the peer sampling?

excerpts.author: fradamt
excerpts.content: Nothing changes, we need a minimum of 8 samples, obtained in whatever way

excerpts.author: fradamt
excerpts.content: How would people feel about increasing `BALANCE_PER_ADDITIONAL_CUSTODY_GROUP`, say to 128 or 256, pushing up quite a bit the minimum stake to be a backbone node (I'll try for a bit with this <:crazycry:932693133546889216>), and making the impact even lower on nodes without a lot of validators? (e.g. with 128 you'd need at least 1024 ETH to go over the minimum of 8 columns, and you'd need 512 validators to be a backbone node)

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: In general I believe this is a good idea, previous to CSM the stake distribution of nodes was bimodal, with either 1-2 or really a lot. I suspect that CSM may have changed this slightly. At any rate my interest on the topic is that this numbers allow us to do statistics on the number of nodes that are expected to hold all columns and use this on our basic assumptions about DA, I know it's not as theoretically robust as saying there are x% chances that > 50% were assigned missing data, but I still think that this is just the same for all practical purposes.

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: seems generally reasonable/positive. the discourse around this has been usually assuming a mostly, yeah, bimodal distribution, and this would push things towards that being descriptively true

excerpts.author: tersec
